article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Morning Brief
article.dek: Quarterback changes are defining Week 3, while the newest NFL EDGE card keeps three plays in place and raises Seattle's recommended stake.

items.headline: Week 3 is already moving at quarterback
paragraphs: Washington will start Marcus Mariota against Seattle after Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow. Minnesota gets Kyler Murray back after he cleared concussion protocol, and Atlanta will start Michael Penix Jr. on Thursday night against Green Bay in his first start since last season's knee injury.

Two other injuries are worth watching across the slate. Colts receiver Alec Pierce is expected to miss several weeks after aggravating his heel injury, and Rams coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua's status for Sunday at Denver remains to be determined after Nacua missed Monday night with a hip injury.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Seattle and Minnesota have clearer quarterback context
paragraphs: Seattle moneyline and Minnesota moneyline are both on the newest NFL EDGE card, so the quarterback news matters directly. Washington is committed to Mariota, while Murray's clearance removes a major uncertainty from Minnesota's matchup.

That does not mean chasing either side if the sportsbook price runs away. The current Play Through is still the guardrail: Seattle is playable through -309 and Minnesota through -123 on the newest verified card.

items.headline: Seattle is popular, but the market is moving with the crowd
paragraphs: This is a broad public-betting/line-movement signal, not a DraftKings-vs-Circa split. Action Network currently shows roughly 87% of spread bets on Seattle, while the listed market has moved from Seattle -3.5 at open to around -7.5. That is a big move in the same direction as the public betting, not a market pushing back against it.
Minnesota and Las Vegas look similar: the listed movement is broadly aligned with the side attracting more spread bets. That leaves no useful contrarian disagreement to exploit this morning.
items.takeaway: Do not manufacture a Fade. For Seattle, use the NFL EDGE moneyline price instead: the last verified recommendation is DraftKings -298, playable through -309. If the price moves beyond that, pass rather than chase.

items.headline: Seattle's stake increased; Minnesota and Las Vegas held
paragraphs: Seattle moneyline is still DraftKings -298 and playable through -309, but NFL EDGE raised the recommended stake from 0.5u to 0.75u. Minnesota moneyline remains DraftKings -120, playable through -123 for 0.75u. Las Vegas +3 remains DraftKings +102, playable through -101 for 0.75u.
Compared with the immediately preceding card, the Seattle sizing change is the only update. The sides, books and listed prices for Minnesota and Las Vegas did not change.
items.takeaway: Treat the Seattle move as a sizing update, not permission to pay any price. Stay inside -309.

items.headline: More confidence does not erase the price limit
paragraphs: A larger recommended stake and a Play Through answer different questions. Stake size tells you how much exposure NFL EDGE wants at an acceptable number; Play Through tells you when the number has become too expensive. If the stake rises but the market crosses Play Through, the answer is still pass.

evidence.fact: Dedicated VSiN DraftKings and Circa NFL split surfaces were checked first, but the accessible pages did not establish a reliable current game-specific DK-vs-Circa comparison for Seattle, Minnesota or Las Vegas. Action Network's current NFL public-betting board showed about 87% of spread bets on Seattle with the listed line moving from Seattle -3.5 to around -7.5, about 64% on Minnesota with the market moving from Minnesota +1.5 to around -1.5, and about 57% on Las Vegas with the line around +3 after opening +3.5. The article therefore labels this as broad public betting plus line movement, not a DK-vs-Circa split, and reports no useful Fade disagreement.
